claims.claim: Lsd1 may be a point of vulnerability for acute myeloid leukemia cells.
claims.source: In addition, recent evidence suggests that Lsd1 may be a point of vulnerability for acute myeloid leukemia cells (Harris et al., 2012; Schenk et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is based on recent studies cited.

claims.claim: Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals were born at Mendelian ratios.
claims.source: Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals were born at Mendelian ratios, but died neonatally of severe anemia (Figure 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals died neonatally of severe anemia.
claims.source: Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals were born at Mendelian ratios, but died neonatally of severe anemia (Figure 1A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claims.claim: Deletion of Lsd1 during embryonic development was incomplete in Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals, as evidenced by the presence of Lsd1 protein in knockout and control fetal liver (FL) lysates.
claims.source: Deletion of Lsd1 during embryonic development was incomplete, as evidenced by the presence of Lsd1 protein in knockout and control fetal liver (FL) lysates (Figure 1C), precluding analysis of embryonic hematopoiesis.
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Lsd1 protein was completely absent in newborn Lsd1fl/fl VavCre bone marrow samples.
claims.source: We could, however, study fetal hematopoiesis since Lsd1 protein was completely absent in newborn Lsd1fl/fl VavCre bone marrow (BM) samples (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Blood counts of Lsd1fl/fl VavCre newborns were significantly reduced.
claims.source: Blood counts of Lsd1fl/fl VavCre newborns were significantly reduced (Figure 1D,E), as was total BM but not FL cellularity (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claims.claim: Total BM cellularity was reduced in Lsd1fl/fl VavCre newborns.
claims.source: Blood counts of Lsd1fl/fl VavCre newborns were significantly reduced (Figure 1D,E), as was total BM but not FL cellularity (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: FL cellularity was not reduced in Lsd1fl/fl VavCre newborns.
claims.source: Blood counts of Lsd1fl/fl VavCre newborns were significantly reduced (Figure 1D,E), as was total BM but not FL cellularity (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: The hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell compartment of Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals was vastly distorted.
claims.source: These findings are indicative of defects in the most immature bone marrow cells. Indeed, the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell compartment of Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals was vastly distorted (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: Frequency and absolute numbers of lineage-negative Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells (LS+K+) were reduced over 30-fold in Lsd1fl/lf VavCre mice.
claims.source: Frequency and absolute numbers of lineage-negative Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells (i.e., LS+K+; encompassing hematopoietic stem cells and multipotent progenitors [MPP]) as well as lineage-negative Sca-1− c-Kit+ cells (LS−K+ cells; encompassing myeloid progenitor cells) were reduced over 30-fold in Lsd1fl/lf VavCre mice (Figure 1H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: Frequency and absolute numbers of lineage-negative Sca-1− c-Kit+ cells (LS−K+) were reduced over 30-fold in Lsd1fl/lf VavCre mice.
claims.source: Frequency and absolute numbers of lineage-negative Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells (i.e., LS+K+; encompassing hematopoietic stem cells and multipotent progenitors [MPP]) as well as lineage-negative Sca-1− c-Kit+ cells (LS−K+ cells; encompassing myeloid progenitor cells) were reduced over 30-fold in Lsd1fl/lf VavCre mice (Figure 1H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: The only cell population present in the lineage-negative compartment of Lsd1fl/fl VavCre mice consisted of Sca-1+ c-Kit− cells (LS+K− cells).
claims.source: The only cell population present in the lineage-negative compartment consisted of Sca-1+ c-Kit− cells (LS+K− cells, a poorly defined population, which may contain early lymphoid cells; Harman et al., 2008; Kumar et al., 2008; Brickshawana et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data.

claims.claim: Injection of Lsd1fl/fl and Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice with the dsRNA poly(I:C) resulted in efficient Lsd1 inactivation.
claims.source: Injection of Lsd1fl/fl and Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice with the dsRNA poly(I:C) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) resulted in efficient Lsd1 inactivation and a massive reduction in peripheral blood counts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot and PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Injection of Lsd1fl/fl and Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice with the dsRNA poly(I:C) resulted in a massive reduction in peripheral blood counts.
claims.source: Injection of Lsd1fl/fl and Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice with the dsRNA poly(I:C) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) resulted in efficient Lsd1 inactivation and a massive reduction in peripheral blood counts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by blood count data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-D.

claims.claim: The majority of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice died with severe anemia 7–10 days after the final poly(I:C) dose.
claims.source: In keeping with this, the majority of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice died with severe anemia 7–10 days after the final dose (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre animals were largely deficient in LS+K+ as well as LS−K+ cells.
claims.source: As in Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre animals were largely deficient in LS+K+ as well as LS−K+ cells, again at the expense of LS+K− cells (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The frequency of Lsd1 knockout lin− CD150+ CD48− Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells was increased about fourfold.
claims.source: Interestingly, the frequency of Lsd1 knockout lin− CD150+ CD48− Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells was increased about fourfold (p≤0.001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Twice as many Lsd1 knockout lin− CD150+ CD48− Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells were proliferating compared to Lsd1fl/fl cells.
claims.source: In keeping with this, we found that twice as many Lsd1 knockout lin− CD150+ CD48− Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells were proliferating, and their apoptosis levels were not significantly altered compared to Lsd1fl/fl cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Apoptosis levels of Lsd1 knockout lin− CD150+ CD48− Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells were not significantly altered compared to Lsd1fl/fl cells.
claims.source: In keeping with this, we found that twice as many Lsd1 knockout lin− CD150+ CD48− Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells were proliferating, and their apoptosis levels were not significantly altered compared to Lsd1fl/fl cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by apoptosis analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre LT-HSCs clustered closest with wild-type LT-HSCs in single cell qPCR analysis.
claims.source: Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre LT-HSCs clustered closest with wild-type LT-HSCs, further substantiating that knockout lin− CD150+ CD48− Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells represent authentic LT-HSCs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,F; LT-HSC cluster).
claims.evidence: This is supported by single cell qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claims.claim: Control LT-HSCs generated large colonies of multipotential granulocyte, erythroid, macrophage, and megakaryocyte progenitor identity (CFU-GEMM) in methylcellulose assays.
claims.source: Control LT-HSCs generated large colonies of multipotential granulocyte, erythroid, macrophage, and megakaryocyte progenitor identity (CFU-GEMM), whereas Lsd1-deficient colonies were smaller and consisted almost exclusively of immature blasts.
claims.evidence: This is supported by colony assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Lsd1-deficient LT-HSC colonies were smaller and consisted almost exclusively of immature blasts.
claims.source: Control LT-HSCs generated large colonies of multipotential granulocyte, erythroid, macrophage, and megakaryocyte progenitor identity (CFU-GEMM), whereas Lsd1-deficient colonies were smaller and consisted almost exclusively of immature blasts.
claims.evidence: This is supported by colony assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Lsd1 knockout colonies primarily consisted of lineage-negative c-Kit+ Sca-1+ hematopoietic progenitor cells.
claims.source: Lsd1 knockout colonies primarily consisted of lineage-negative c-Kit+ Sca-1+ hematopoietic progenitor cells, whereas wild-type colonies were largely composed of mature Gr1+ Mac1+ myeloid cells (Figure 2E,G–J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2E,G-J.

claims.claim: Wild-type LT-HSC colonies were largely composed of mature Gr1+ Mac1+ myeloid cells.
claims.source: Lsd1 knockout colonies primarily consisted of lineage-negative c-Kit+ Sca-1+ hematopoietic progenitor cells, whereas wild-type colonies were largely composed of mature Gr1+ Mac1+ myeloid cells (Figure 2E,G–J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2E,G-J.

claims.claim: Lsd1 function is vital for efficient differentiation of LT-HSCs into more mature myeloid progenitor cells.
claims.source: Together, the absence of LS−K+ myeloid progenitors determined by flow cytometry, the single cell multiplex qPCR immunoprofiling data, and colony assays indicate that Lsd1 function is vital for efficient differentiation of LT-HSCs into more mature myeloid progenitor cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from multiple lines of experimental evidence including flow cytometry, qPCR, and colony assays.

claims.claim: By 4 weeks after poly(I:C), the contribution of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells to the myeloid lineage was barely detectable in competitive transplantation experiments.
claims.source: By 4 weeks after poly(I:C), the contribution of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells to the myeloid lineage was barely detectable and remained low for 12 weeks (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transplantation data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The contribution of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells to the B and T lymphoid lineages decreased >50% at 4 weeks after poly(I:C) and progressively declined over 12 weeks in competitive transplantation experiments.
claims.source: Correspondingly, the contribution of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells to the B and T lymphoid lineages decreased >50% at 4 weeks after poly(I:C) and progressively declined over 12 weeks (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transplantation data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: At 12 weeks after poly(I:C) injection, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells generated only 2–14% of mature cells in the spleen.
claims.source: Likewise, at 12 weeks after poly(I:C) injection, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells generated only 2–14% of mature cells in the spleen and 1–9% of mature cells in the bone marrow (Figure 3C,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transplantation data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claims.claim: At 12 weeks after poly(I:C) injection, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells generated 1–9% of mature cells in the bone marrow.
claims.source: Likewise, at 12 weeks after poly(I:C) injection, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells generated only 2–14% of mature cells in the spleen and 1–9% of mature cells in the bone marrow (Figure 3C,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transplantation data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claims.claim: 12 weeks after poly(I:C) treatment, the level of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells that contributed to lineage-negative CD150+ Sca-1+ c-Kit+ hematopoietic stem cells was virtually undetectable.
claims.source: 12 weeks after poly(I:C) treatment, the level of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells that either contributed to lineage-negative CD150+ Sca-1+ c-Kit+ hematopoietic stem cells, CD150− LS+K+ multipotent progenitor cells, or various lineage-negative myeloid progenitor cells (i.e., GMP, PreGM, PreMegE, MkP, PreCFU-E, CFU-E) was virtually undetectable (Figure 3E,F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by transplantation data shown in Figure 3E,F.

claims.claim: Lsd1 is a crucial epigenetic guardian of HSC self-renewal and homeostasis.
claims.source: In combination, these data implicate Lsd1 as crucial epigenetic guardian of HSC self-renewal and homeostasis.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the transplantation experiments showing loss of Lsd1-deficient HSCs.

claims.claim: Mature Gr1high Mac1+ granulocytes were almost absent from the bone marrow of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice.
claims.source: Indeed, mature Gr1high Mac1+ granulocytes were almost absent from the bone marrow of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: The concomitant accumulation of immature Gr1dim Mac1+ cells in Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice indicated a defect in granulocytic maturation.
claims.source: The concomitant accumulation of immature Gr1dim Mac1+ cells, a population containing immature granulocytes, bipotential granulocytic/monocytic precursor cells, and monocytes (Hestdal et al., 1991; Walkley et al., 2002), indicated a defect in granulocytic maturation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the flow cytometry data showing accumulation of immature cells.

claims.claim: Loss of Lsd1 culminates in a differentiation block at the transition of immature Gr1dim Mac1+ to mature Gr1high Mac1+ granulocytes.
claims.source: Thus, loss of Lsd1 culminates in a differentiation block at the transition of immature Gr1dim Mac1+ to mature Gr1high Mac1+ granulocytes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the flow cytometry and cytospin data showing loss of mature granulocytes and accumulation of immature cells.

claims.claim: EpoRCre-mediated deletion of Lsd1 was lethal in the prenatal period.
claims.source: As EpoRCre-mediated deletion of Lsd1 was lethal in the prenatal period, we analyzed Lsd1fl/fl EpoRCre embryos.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the observation that Lsd1fl/fl EpoRCre embryos could only be analyzed during embryonic development.

claims.claim: Lsd1 knockout embryos displayed a 300% increase of CD71high Ter119low proerythroblasts (R2).
claims.source: Lsd1 knockout embryos displayed a 300% increase of CD71high Ter119low proerythroblasts (R2), but a 20-fold reduction of reticulocytes and erythrocytes (R5; Figure 4D,E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claims.claim: Lsd1 knockout embryos displayed a 20-fold reduction of reticulocytes and erythrocytes (R5).
claims.source: Lsd1 knockout embryos displayed a 300% increase of CD71high Ter119low proerythroblasts (R2), but a 20-fold reduction of reticulocytes and erythrocytes (R5; Figure 4D,E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D,E.

claims.claim: Erythroid cell maturation in Lsd1-deficient embryos is impaired at the transition from proerythroblasts/R2 to basophilic erythroblasts/R3.
claims.source: Thus, erythroid cell maturation in Lsd1-deficient embryos is impaired at the transition from proerythroblasts/R2 to basophilic erythroblasts/R3.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the flow cytometry data showing accumulation of R2 cells and loss of later stage cells.

claims.claim: Enucleated mature definitive erythroid cells were markedly reduced in Lsd1-deficient fetal livers.
claims.source: In keeping with this, enucleated mature definitive erythroid cells were markedly reduced in Lsd1-deficient fetal livers (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by blood smear data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Lsd1-deficient embryos were small and exhibited pale fetal livers at E13.5.
claims.source: Overall, Lsd1-deficient embryos were small and exhibited pale fetal livers at E13.5, similarly consistent with compromised erythropoiesis (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by embryo images shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Lsd1 is essential for terminal granulocytic and erythroid differentiation.
claims.source: Taken together, these data demonstrate that Lsd1 is essential not only for differentiation and self-renewal of hematopoietic stem cells but also for terminal granulocytic and erythroid differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the combined data showing differentiation defects in both granulocytic and erythroid lineages.

claims.claim: Several genes that are typically highly expressed in normal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells were substantially upregulated in Lsd1 mutant cells.
claims.source: Several genes that are typically highly expressed in normal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells were substantially upregulated in Lsd1 mutant cells (e.g., CD34, 41-fold; HoxA9, 35-fold; Sca-1, 16-fold; Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by gene expression profiling data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The stem/progenitor cell gene signature was highly enriched across all of the assayed Lsd1-deficient cells.
claims.source: Strikingly, the stem/progenitor cell gene signature was highly enriched across all of the assayed Lsd1-deficient cells (Figure 5A–C; Gr1dim Mac1+ cells: NES: −2.1; FDR ≤ 10−4; CD71+c-Kit+ proerythroblasts: NES: −2.2; FDR ≤ 10−4; CD150+ CD48− LS+K+ HSCs: NES: −2.0; FDR ≤ 10−4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5A-C.

claims.claim: mRNA expression levels of master transcription factors C/EBPα and Gata1 were not downregulated in Gr1dim Mac1+ cells or in CD71+c-Kit+ proerythroblasts.
claims.source: However, mRNA expression levels of these master transcription factors were not downregulated in Gr1dim Mac1+ cells or in CD71+c-Kit+ proerythroblasts, indicating that the block in terminal differentiation could not be ascribed simply to the reduced expression of these regulators (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Hox genes were significantly upregulated in Lsd1 knockout cells.
claims.source: In order to identify signaling pathways that potentially drive or maintain the upregulation of a stem and progenitor cell gene signature, we again performed gene set enrichment analysis and found that Hox genes, which are typically associated with early hematopoiesis, were significantly upregulated in Lsd1 knockout cells (NES: −1.46; FDR ≤ 0.02; Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: There was significant enrichment of HoxA7-driven (Z-score: 2.746; p=1.63 × 10−8) and HoxA9-driven (Z-score: 2.314; p=1.13 × 10−3) gene expression networks in Lsd1 knockout cells.
claims.source: In keeping with this, we discovered significant enrichment of HoxA7-driven (Z-score: 2.746; p=1.63 × 10−8) and HoxA9-driven (Z-score: 2.314; p=1.13 × 10−3) gene expression networks (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D) by performing pathway enrichment analysis with the 'Ingenuity Systems' pathway analysis tool.
claims.evidence: This is supported by pathway analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The expression of downstream HoxA9 target genes, including Bcl2, Msi2, and Sox4, were significantly upregulated in Lsd1 knockout cells.
claims.source: We found that the expression of downstream HoxA9 target genes, including Bcl2, Msi2, and Sox4, were also significantly upregulated (NES: −1.78; FDR ≤ 0.001; Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: Failure to repress earlier lineage gene expression programs impairs early, as well as later, hematopoietic maturation programs.
claims.source: Based on these findings, we hypothesized that failure to repress earlier lineage gene expression programs impairs early, as well as later, hematopoietic maturation programs.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the gene expression data showing upregulation of stem/progenitor genes in differentiated cells.

claims.claim: A total of 25,173 Lsd1 binding sites (peaks) were identified from the ChIP-Seq data set in 32D cells.
claims.source: In total, we identified a total of 25,173 Lsd1 binding sites (peaks) from the ChIP-Seq data set.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data analysis.

claims.claim: 16 out of 18 (>85%) Lsd1 binding sites identified in 32D cells were also occupied by Lsd1 in primary Gr1dim Mac1+ cells.
claims.source: We chose 18 peaks for validation by ChIP-qPCR in primary Gr1dim Mac1+ cells. We found that 16 (>85%) of these binding sites were also occupied by Lsd1 in Gr1dim Mac1+ cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-qPCR validation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Lsd1 binding peaks were predominantly positioned at intergenic (40%) and intronic (38%) regions.
claims.source: Genome-wide analysis of Lsd1 peak distribution revealed only limited binding to proximal promoters (15%). Lsd1 binding peaks were predominantly positioned at intergenic (40%) and intronic (38%) regions (Figure 5G; Figure 5—source data 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claims.claim: Lsd1 occupied 55% of genes (i.e., 1361 out of 2473) that were at least 1.5-fold (p≥0.05) upregulated in Lsd1 knockout cells.
claims.source: Next, we compared the Lsd1 ChIP-Seq binding sites with gene expression changes extracted from Gr1dim Mac1+ microarray data and found that Lsd1 occupied 55% of genes (i.e., 1361 out of 2473) that were at least 1.5-fold (p≥0.05) upregulated in Lsd1 knockout cells (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by integrative analysis of ChIP-Seq and microarray data shown in Figure 5H.

claims.claim: No differences in global H3K4me1/me2 and H3K9me1/me2 methylation levels were detected between wild-type and Lsd1 knockout cells by Western blot.
claims.source: To assess the potential consequences of Lsd1 loss on global histone methylation levels, we analyzed Lsd1 substrates H3K4me1/me2 and H3K9me1/me2 by Western blot. No differences in global methylation levels were detected (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Lsd1 occupied about three times more putative enhancers than active promoters.
claims.source: Peak overlap analysis of Lsd1 with the respective histone methylation marks confirmed that Lsd1 occupied about three times more putative enhancers (Figure 6B) than active promoters (Figure 6A), implying that Lsd1 in fact regulates both promoter and enhancer activities.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq overlap analysis shown in Figure 6A,B.

claims.claim: Both KO-specific promoter and enhancer peak target genes correlated highly with genes upregulated in Lsd1 knockout Gr1dim Mac1+ cells.
claims.source: We mapped cell type–specific peaks to the nearest Refseq annotated genes (Figure 6—source data 1) and observed that both KO-specific promoter and enhancer peak target genes correlated highly with genes upregulated in Lsd1 knockout Gr1dim Mac1+ cells (Figure 6C,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by integrative analysis shown in Figure 6C,D.

claims.claim: Lsd1 represses gene expression in association with changes in H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 levels at enhancers and promoters, respectively.
claims.source: These findings indicate that Lsd1 represses gene expression in association with changes in H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 levels at enhancers and promoters, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between KO-specific histone marks and gene upregulation.

claims.claim: KO-specific enhancer-associated H3K4me1 (ES: 2.31; p=4.5 × 10−14) peak target genes were highly enriched among the LSK signature genes.
claims.source: We found that both KO-specific enhancer-associated H3K4me1 (ES: 2.31; p=4.5 × 10−14) and the promoter-associated H3K4me2 (ES: 2.60; p=9.7 × 10−19) peak target genes were highly enriched among the LSK signature genes (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: KO-specific promoter-associated H3K4me2 (ES: 2.60; p=9.7 × 10−19) peak target genes were highly enriched among the LSK signature genes.
claims.source: We found that both KO-specific enhancer-associated H3K4me1 (ES: 2.31; p=4.5 × 10−14) and the promoter-associated H3K4me2 (ES: 2.60; p=9.7 × 10−19) peak target genes were highly enriched among the LSK signature genes (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: KO-specific peak target genes were not meaningfully enriched in the granulocyte gene signature.
claims.source: As expected, KO-specific peak target genes were not meaningfully enriched in the granulocyte gene signature (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: Genes that had Lsd1 bound at distal sites and at the promoter were highly enriched (ES: 2.02; p=2.53 × 10−11) in the LSK signature.
claims.source: We found that genes of group (1) were highly enriched (ES: 2.02; p=2.53 × 10−11) and that genes of group (2) were slightly but significantly enriched (ES: 1.15; p=0.02) in the LSK signature.
claims.evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: Genes that had Lsd1 bound only at distal regions were slightly but significantly enriched (ES: 1.15; p=0.02) in the LSK signature.
claims.source: We found that genes of group (1) were highly enriched (ES: 2.02; p=2.53 × 10−11) and that genes of group (2) were slightly but significantly enriched (ES: 1.15; p=0.02) in the LSK signature.
claims.evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: None of the three Lsd1 binding groups were significantly enriched in the granulocyte signature.
claims.source: As expected, none of the three groups were significantly enriched in the granulocyte signature (Figure 6G), suggesting that Lsd1 is directly involved in the repression of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell genes but not in the activation of mature granulocyte genes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: Lsd1 is directly involved in the repression of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell genes but not in the activation of mature granulocyte genes.
claims.source: As expected, none of the three groups were significantly enriched in the granulocyte signature (Figure 6G), suggesting that Lsd1 is directly involved in the repression of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell genes but not in the activation of mature granulocyte genes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment analysis showing selective enrichment in LSK but not granulocyte signatures.

claims.claim: Among the genes occupied by Lsd1 at distal sites and at the promoter were Meis1, Gfi1b, Myb, β-catenin, and Runx1.
claims.source: Among the genes occupied by Lsd1 at distal sites and at the promoter were Meis1, Gfi1b, Myb, β-catenin, and Runx1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A; Figure 6—source data 2), a set of genes with established roles in hematopoietic stem cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data analysis.

claims.claim: Lsd1 occupies distal regulatory regions as well as proximal promoters of stem and progenitor cell genes.
claims.source: Collectively, we established that Lsd1 occupies distal regulatory regions as well as proximal promoters of stem and progenitor cell genes and that deletion of Lsd1 is associated with increased levels of the Lsd1 substrates H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 on enhancers and promoters of HSPC genes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data showing Lsd1 occupancy at both enhancers and promoters.

claims.claim: Deletion of Lsd1 is associated with increased levels of the Lsd1 substrates H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 on enhancers and promoters of HSPC genes.
claims.source: Collectively, we established that Lsd1 occupies distal regulatory regions as well as proximal promoters of stem and progenitor cell genes and that deletion of Lsd1 is associated with increased levels of the Lsd1 substrates H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 on enhancers and promoters of HSPC genes.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data comparing wild-type and knockout cells.

claims.claim: Conditional deletion of Lsd1 resulted in severe pancytopenia.
claims.source: Through study of blood lineage–specific conditional knockout mice, we established that Lsd1 is an indispensable factor for hematopoietic differentiation. Conditional deletion of Lsd1 resulted in severe pancytopenia, the consequence of combined defects in early hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and terminal blood cell maturation.
claims.evidence: This is supported by blood count data from conditional knockout mice.

claims.claim: Lsd1 is an indispensable factor for hematopoietic differentiation.
claims.source: Through study of blood lineage–specific conditional knockout mice, we established that Lsd1 is an indispensable factor for hematopoietic differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion based on all experimental data from conditional knockout mice.

claims.claim: Lsd1 is crucial for immature hematopoietic stem cell differentiation.
claims.source: We established that Lsd1 is crucial not only for immature hematopoietic stem cell differentiation, as might have been expected from the previous ES cell studies (Wang et al., 2009a; Adamo et al., 2011; Whyte et al., 2012), but also critical for differentiation of mature hematopoietic cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by HSC differentiation assays and transplantation experiments.

claims.claim: Lsd1 is critical for differentiation of mature hematopoietic cells.
claims.source: We established that Lsd1 is crucial not only for immature hematopoietic stem cell differentiation, as might have been expected from the previous ES cell studies (Wang et al., 2009a; Adamo et al., 2011; Whyte et al., 2012), but also critical for differentiation of mature hematopoietic cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by terminal differentiation defects in granulocytic and erythroid lineages.

claims.claim: Lsd1-deficient HSCs were severely impaired in their capacity to mature into immature progenitors.
claims.source: Taken together, we found that Lsd1-deficient HSCs were severely impaired in their capacity to mature into immature progenitors.
claims.evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry and colony assay data.

claims.claim: Deletion of Lsd1 strongly interfered with terminal granulocytic and erythroid differentiation.
claims.source: Deletion of Lsd1 not only compromised early hematopoietic differentiation but also strongly interfered with terminal granulocytic and erythroid differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is supported by data showing differentiation blocks in both granulocytic and erythroid lineages.

claims.claim: Differentiating Lsd1 knockout cells aberrantly express HSPC genes normally expressed only in HSCs and progenitors.
claims.source: As a consequence, differentiating Lsd1 knockout cells aberrantly express HSPC genes normally expressed only in HSCs and progenitors.
claims.evidence: This is supported by gene expression profiling data showing upregulation of HSPC genes in differentiated cells.

claims.claim: Failure to silence LSK-associated genes in Lsd1 mutants interferes with proper differentiation.
claims.source: We propose that failure to silence these LSK-associated genes in Lsd1 mutants interferes with proper differentiation, culminating in detrimental consequences for hematopoiesis (see Figure 7 for model).
claims.evidence: This is the proposed model based on all experimental findings.

claims.claim: Chemical inhibition of Lsd1 enzymatic activity resulted in increased apoptosis and impaired leukemogenicity of MLL-AF9- and PML-RARα-transformed cells.
claims.source: These studies described that chemical inhibition of the enzymatic activity, as well as knockdown of Lsd1, resulted in increased apoptosis and impaired leukemogenicity of MLL-AF9- and PML-RARα-transformed cells (Harris et al., 2012; Schenk et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is based on previous studies cited.

claims.claim: RNAi-mediated or chemical inhibition of Lsd1 enhances γ-globin expression in human erythroid cells.
claims.source: Two independent studies have described that RNAi-mediated or chemical inhibition of Lsd1 enhances γ-globin expression in human erythroid cells and quite modestly in human β-locus transgenic mice (Shi et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2013), which would alleviate symptoms of β-hemoglobinopathies such as sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia.
claims.evidence: This is based on previous studies cited.

claims.claim: Appreciable or complete inhibition of Lsd1 could have undesired side effects.
claims.source: Although these findings illustrate favorable features of Lsd1 as a potential drug target, Sprüssel et al. (2012), Xu et al., and this study demonstrate that Lsd1 serves critical roles in hematopoietic differentiation and that appreciable or complete inhibition of Lsd1 could have undesired side effects.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the severe hematopoietic defects observed upon Lsd1 deletion.

claims.claim: Lsd1 occupies only about 30% of active enhancers in mature myeloid cells.
claims.source: Lsd1-occupancy data generated from murine and human embryonic stem cells suggested that Lsd1 occupies and regulates virtually all enhancers of embryonic stem cell genes (Ram et al., 2011; Whyte et al., 2012), whereas our data interestingly reveal that Lsd1 occupies only about 30% of active enhancers in mature myeloid cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by ChIP-Seq data analysis comparing Lsd1 occupancy with enhancer marks.

claims.claim: ES cell chromatin exists in an unique and unusual configuration with widely dispersed open chromatin.
claims.source: In this regard, it is relevant to recall that ES cell chromatin exists in an unique and unusual configuration with widely dispersed open chromatin (Efroni et al., 2008), and that following differentiation, there is extensive epigenetic reorganization (Meshorer and Misteli, 2006; Efroni et al., 2008; Hiratani et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies cited.

claims.claim: Following ES cell differentiation, there is extensive epigenetic reorganization.
claims.source: In this regard, it is relevant to recall that ES cell chromatin exists in an unique and unusual configuration with widely dispersed open chromatin (Efroni et al., 2008), and that following differentiation, there is extensive epigenetic reorganization (Meshorer and Misteli, 2006; Efroni et al., 2008; Hiratani et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies cited.

claims.claim: The epigenetic profile of fetal blood cells differs from adult blood cells.
claims.source: Recent genome-wide comparisons between fetal and adult hematopoietic cells have illustrated how the epigenetic profile of fetal blood cells differs from adult blood cells (Xu et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is based on a previous study cited.

claims.claim: There is a differential requirement for Lsd1 in ES cells vs mature cells.
claims.source: In light of the global differences in the architecture of embryonic, fetal, and adult epigenetic landscapes, it is noteworthy that our data suggest a somewhat differential requirement for Lsd1 in ES cells vs mature cells, and hence open new avenues to study how other histone demethylases, or other chromatin remodeling factors, participate in the regulation of enhancers during adult tissue differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from comparing the current data with previous ES cell studies.

claims.claim: Loss of Lsd1 protein has been suggested to destabilize the CoREST complex.
claims.source: For example, loss of Lsd1 protein has been suggested to destabilize the CoREST complex (Lee et al., 2005; Foster et al., 2010), which has been demonstrated to result in increased global H3K56 acetylation (Foster et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is based on previous studies cited.

claims.claim: Destabilization of the CoREST complex results in increased global H3K56 acetylation.
claims.source: For example, loss of Lsd1 protein has been suggested to destabilize the CoREST complex (Lee et al., 2005; Foster et al., 2010), which has been demonstrated to result in increased global H3K56 acetylation (Foster et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is based on a previous study cited.

claims.claim: Lsd1 is essential for the stability of DNA methyltransferase 1 (Dnmt1).
claims.source: Lsd1 is also essential for the stability of DNA methyltransferase 1 (Dnmt1; Wang et al., 2009a).
claims.evidence: This is based on a previous study cited.

claims.claim: Conditional Dnmt1 knockout animals show subtle hematopoietic phenotypes during steady-state hematopoiesis.
claims.source: However, given the subtle hematopoietic phenotypes observed in conditional Dnmt1 knockout animals during steady-state hematopoiesis (Bröske et al., 2009; Trowbridge et al., 2009), we believe this to be unlikely.
claims.evidence: This is based on previous studies cited.

claims.claim: Lsd1 is an epigenetic governor required broadly for repression of stem cell gene expression programs during embryonic stem cell as well as somatic cell differentiation.
claims.source: Collectively, we identified Lsd1 as indispensible for hematopoietic differentiation. We propose that Lsd1 is an epigenetic governor required broadly for repression of stem cell gene expression programs during embryonic stem cell as well as somatic cell differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion integrating findings from this study with previous ES cell studies.

claims.claim: The possibility of Lsd1 as a potential drug target in hematopoietic malignancies will have to be carefully evaluated in the context of potentially detrimental side effects.
claims.source: Given its crucial role in hematopoietic differentiation, the possibility of Lsd1 as a potential drug target in hematopoietic malignancies will have to be carefully evaluated in the context of potentially detrimental side effects.
claims.evidence: This is a cautionary statement based on the severe hematopoietic defects observed upon Lsd1 deletion.

results.result: Lsd1fl/fl VavCre animals were born at Mendelian ratios but died neonatally of severe anemia. Deletion of Lsd1 during embryonic development was incomplete in fetal liver but complete in newborn bone marrow. Blood counts and bone marrow cellularity were significantly reduced, and the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell compartment was vastly distorted with >30-fold reduction in LS+K+ and LS-K+ cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C34 are well-supported by Western blot data (C26, C27), blood count data (C28), cellularity measurements (C29, C30), and flow cytometry analysis (C31-C34) shown in Figure 1. The data consistently demonstrate severe hematopoietic defects in VavCre-mediated Lsd1 deletion.

results.result: Poly(I:C) injection in Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice resulted in efficient Lsd1 inactivation, massive reduction in peripheral blood counts, and death within 7-10 days. Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre animals were largely deficient in LS+K+ and LS-K+ cells. The frequency of lin- CD150+ CD48- Sca-1+ c-Kit+ cells increased fourfold with twice as many cells proliferating, and these cells clustered with wild-type LT-HSCs in single cell qPCR analysis.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C42 are supported by Western blot and PCR data (C35), blood count data (C36), survival data (C37), flow cytometry (C38, C39), cell cycle analysis (C40, C41), and single cell qPCR clustering (C42) shown in Figure 2 and supplementary figures. The data demonstrate efficient Lsd1 deletion and severe hematopoietic defects in the Mx1Cre system.

results.result: In methylcellulose colony assays, control LT-HSCs generated large CFU-GEMM colonies, whereas Lsd1-deficient colonies were smaller and consisted almost exclusively of immature blasts. Lsd1 knockout colonies primarily consisted of lineage-negative c-Kit+ Sca-1+ hematopoietic progenitor cells, while wild-type colonies were largely composed of mature Gr1+ Mac1+ myeloid cells. These data indicate that Lsd1 function is vital for efficient differentiation of LT-HSCs into more mature myeloid progenitor cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C47 are supported by colony assay morphology data (C43, C44) and flow cytometry analysis of colony composition (C45, C46) shown in Figure 2D-J. The conclusion (C47) is appropriately inferred from multiple converging lines of evidence including flow cytometry, qPCR, and colony assays.

results.result: In competitive bone marrow transplantation experiments, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells showed severely reduced contribution to myeloid lineages (barely detectable at 4 weeks), progressive decline in B and T lymphoid lineages (>50% decrease at 4 weeks), and only 2-14% of mature cells in spleen and 1-9% in bone marrow at 12 weeks. At 12 weeks, Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre cells contributing to HSCs and various progenitor populations were virtually undetectable. These data implicate Lsd1 as a crucial epigenetic guardian of HSC self-renewal and homeostasis.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C53 are supported by comprehensive transplantation data shown in Figure 3B-F, demonstrating progressive loss of Lsd1-deficient cells across all hematopoietic lineages and stem/progenitor compartments. The conclusion (C53) is appropriately inferred from the transplantation data showing competitive disadvantage and loss of Lsd1-deficient HSCs.

results.result: Mature Gr1high Mac1+ granulocytes were almost absent from the bone marrow of Lsd1fl/fl Mx1Cre mice, with concomitant accumulation of immature Gr1dim Mac1+ cells. Loss of Lsd1 culminates in a differentiation block at the transition of immature Gr1dim Mac1+ to mature Gr1high Mac1+ granulocytes.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C56 are supported by flow cytometry data (C54) shown in Figure 4A,B and cytospin preparations. The inference of a differentiation block (C56) is appropriately drawn from the accumulation of immature cells and loss of mature granulocytes. However, the manuscript does not provide direct evidence ruling out alternative explanations such as selective survival of immature cells.

results.result: EpoRCre-mediated deletion of Lsd1 was lethal in the prenatal period. Lsd1 knockout embryos displayed a 300% increase of CD71high Ter119low proerythroblasts (R2) but a 20-fold reduction of reticulocytes and erythrocytes (R5). Erythroid cell maturation in Lsd1-deficient embryos is impaired at the transition from proerythroblasts/R2 to basophilic erythroblasts/R3. Enucleated mature definitive erythroid cells were markedly reduced, and embryos were small with pale fetal livers at E13.5. These data demonstrate that Lsd1 is essential for terminal granulocytic and erythroid differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C63 are supported by flow cytometry data (C58, C59) shown in Figure 4D,E, blood smear data (C61), and embryo images (C62). The conclusion (C63) is appropriately inferred from the combined data showing differentiation defects in both granulocytic and erythroid lineages.

results.result: Several genes typically highly expressed in normal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (e.g., CD34, HoxA9, Sca-1) were substantially upregulated in Lsd1 mutant cells. The stem/progenitor cell gene signature was highly enriched across all assayed Lsd1-deficient cells (Gr1dim Mac1+ cells, CD71+c-Kit+ proerythroblasts, CD150+ CD48- LS+K+ HSCs) with highly significant NES scores and FDR values. Hox genes and HoxA9 target genes were significantly upregulated. The authors hypothesize that failure to repress earlier lineage gene expression programs impairs early and later hematopoietic maturation programs.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C69 are supported by gene expression profiling data (C64), GSEA analysis (C65, C67, C69), qPCR data (C66), and pathway analysis (C68) shown in Figure 5 and supplementary figures. The hypothesis (C70) is appropriately labeled as speculation and is based on the gene expression data. The statistical significance is strong with appropriate FDR corrections.

results.result: A total of 25,173 Lsd1 binding sites (peaks) were identified from ChIP-Seq data in 32D cells. 16 out of 18 (>85%) Lsd1 binding sites identified in 32D cells were validated by ChIP-qPCR in primary Gr1dim Mac1+ cells. Lsd1 binding peaks were predominantly positioned at intergenic (40%) and intronic (38%) regions with limited binding to proximal promoters (15%). Lsd1 occupied 55% of genes (1361 out of 2473) that were at least 1.5-fold upregulated in Lsd1 knockout cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C74 are supported by ChIP-Seq data analysis (C71, C73, C74) and ChIP-qPCR validation (C72) shown in Figure 5G-H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A. The validation rate of >85% (C72) provides confidence in the ChIP-Seq data quality. The use of a cell line (32D) for ChIP-Seq is a limitation, but validation in primary cells strengthens the findings.

results.result: No differences in global H3K4me1/me2 and H3K9me1/me2 methylation levels were detected between wild-type and Lsd1 knockout cells by Western blot. Lsd1 occupied about three times more putative enhancers than active promoters. Both KO-specific promoter and enhancer peak target genes correlated highly with genes upregulated in Lsd1 knockout Gr1dim Mac1+ cells. These findings indicate that Lsd1 represses gene expression in association with changes in H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 levels at enhancers and promoters, respectively.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C78 are supported by Western blot data (C75), ChIP-Seq overlap analysis (C76), and integrative analysis (C77) shown in Figure 6A-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B. The conclusion (C78) is appropriately inferred from the correlation between KO-specific histone marks and gene upregulation. The lack of global changes (C75) is important as it indicates Lsd1 acts locally at specific genomic regions.

results.result: KO-specific enhancer-associated H3K4me1 and promoter-associated H3K4me2 peak target genes were highly enriched among the LSK signature genes with highly significant enrichment scores and p-values. KO-specific peak target genes were not meaningfully enriched in the granulocyte gene signature. Genes with Lsd1 bound at distal sites and promoter were highly enriched in the LSK signature, while genes with Lsd1 bound only at distal regions were slightly but significantly enriched. None of the three Lsd1 binding groups were significantly enriched in the granulocyte signature. These data suggest that Lsd1 is directly involved in the repression of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell genes but not in the activation of mature granulocyte genes. Lsd1 occupies distal regulatory regions as well as proximal promoters of stem and progenitor cell genes, and deletion of Lsd1 is associated with increased levels of H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 on enhancers and promoters of HSPC genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C88 are supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6E-G and ChIP-Seq data analysis. The statistical significance is strong with appropriate p-values. The conclusion (C85) is appropriately inferred from the selective enrichment in LSK but not granulocyte signatures. The identification of specific genes (C86) provides biological validation of the findings.

results.result: Conditional deletion of Lsd1 resulted in severe pancytopenia, the consequence of combined defects in early hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and terminal blood cell maturation. Lsd1 is an indispensable factor for hematopoietic differentiation, crucial for immature hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and critical for differentiation of mature hematopoietic cells. Lsd1-deficient HSCs were severely impaired in their capacity to mature into immature progenitors. Deletion of Lsd1 strongly interfered with terminal granulocytic and erythroid differentiation. Differentiating Lsd1 knockout cells aberrantly express HSPC genes normally expressed only in HSCs and progenitors. The authors propose that failure to silence LSK-associated genes in Lsd1 mutants interferes with proper differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C96 represent the main conclusions of the study, integrating findings from all experimental approaches. These conclusions are well-supported by the comprehensive data from conditional knockout mice, transplantation experiments, colony assays, flow cytometry, gene expression profiling, and ChIP-Seq analysis. The proposed model (C96) is appropriately labeled as speculation and is based on all experimental findings.

results.result: Background knowledge claims about Lsd1 biochemical function, histone methylation marks, and chromatin biology. These include Lsd1's demethylase activity on H3K4/K9, the distribution of H3K4 methylation marks at promoters and enhancers, the enzymes that catalyze H3K4 methylation and demethylation, and Lsd1's function in repressor complexes.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C10-C19 are established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies. These claims provide necessary background context for the study but are not novel findings. The citations appear appropriate and the knowledge claims are consistent with the field.

results.result: Prior work on Lsd1 deletion showing embryonic lethality, developmental arrest around E5.5-E7.5, proliferation and differentiation defects in ESCs, and potential vulnerability of acute myeloid leukemia cells to Lsd1 inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C23 are based on previous studies cited in the manuscript. These claims provide important context for the current study by establishing what was known about Lsd1 function prior to this work. The citations appear appropriate.

results.result: Discussion of Lsd1 as a potential drug target in hematopoietic malignancies and β-hemoglobinopathies, with cautionary notes about potential side effects based on the severe hematopoietic defects observed upon Lsd1 deletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C98 are based on previous studies cited. Claims C99 and C110 are appropriately cautious statements inferred from the severe hematopoietic defects observed in this study. The authors appropriately note that appreciable or complete inhibition of Lsd1 could have undesired side effects, which is a reasonable inference from their data.

results.result: Comparison of Lsd1 function in ES cells versus mature myeloid cells, showing that Lsd1 occupies only about 30% of active enhancers in mature myeloid cells compared to virtually all enhancers in ES cells. Discussion of differences in chromatin architecture between ES cells, fetal cells, and adult cells, suggesting a differential requirement for Lsd1 in ES cells versus mature cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C104 are supported by ChIP-Seq data analysis (C100) and established knowledge from previous studies (C101-C103). The inference of differential requirement for Lsd1 (C104) is appropriately drawn from comparing the current data with previous ES cell studies. This represents an important insight about context-dependent Lsd1 function.

results.result: Discussion of potential indirect effects of Lsd1 deletion, including destabilization of the CoREST complex leading to increased H3K56 acetylation, and effects on Dnmt1 stability. The authors note that Dnmt1 knockout animals show subtle hematopoietic phenotypes, making it unlikely that Dnmt1 destabilization accounts for the severe phenotypes observed.
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C108 are based on previous studies cited. The authors appropriately discuss potential indirect effects of Lsd1 deletion and provide reasoning for why Dnmt1 destabilization is unlikely to account for the observed phenotypes. This represents appropriate consideration of alternative explanations.

results.result: Main conclusions of the study: Lsd1 is an indispensible epigenetic governor of hematopoietic differentiation that represses HSPC gene expression programs during hematopoietic differentiation. Lsd1 acts at transcription start sites as well as enhancer regions. Loss of Lsd1 is associated with increased H3K4me1 and H3K4me2 methylation on HSPC genes and gene derepression. Failure to fully silence HSPC genes compromises differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells and mature blood cell lineages. Lsd1-mediated concurrent repression of enhancer and promoter activity of stem and progenitor cell genes is a pivotal epigenetic mechanism required for proper hematopoietic maturation. The authors propose that Lsd1 is an epigenetic governor required broadly for repression of stem cell gene expression programs during embryonic stem cell as well as somatic cell differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C2-C9 and C109 represent the main conclusions of the study, integrating findings from all experimental approaches. These conclusions are well-supported by comprehensive data from conditional knockout mice, transplantation experiments, colony assays, flow cytometry, gene expression profiling, and ChIP-Seq analysis. The proposal that Lsd1 is required broadly for stem cell gene repression (C109) is appropriately labeled as speculation and represents an extrapolation from the hematopoietic data.
